newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mostly higher, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mostly higher, seen stabilising.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly higher in sluggish trade, which saw blue chips gaining further on Thursday, but market watchers branded the lull as temporary.
They predicted no big price changes this week, after a generally upward trend of the past fortnight. However, the market was seen as needing foreign investors for a boost.
"I believe the prices will remain stable," one trader with a large market share told Reuters.
Turnover shrank to 3.6 from 5.5 million kuna on Thursday and volume to 6,852 shares from over 8,000.
Food stock Podravka with 3,530 units sold was the only issue to beat scarce buying. Its shares closed 0.50 kuna higher at 305.50.
"There are no big buyers because foreigners are are waiting to see how things develop in Podunavlje," said Ivan Hren of Ceufin brokers, referring to the last rebel Serb enclave.
The area should see local government bodies reestablished by the end of May after Croatian parties won a majority in the April 13-14 local elections.

Seven of twelve active issues rose on Thursday, four fell and one was flat. The day's gainers were led by Zagrebacka Banka's C-series bearer stock, up 5.5 percent to 850 kuna on a meagre volume of 12 shares.
Its ordinary shares inched up 12.9 kuna to 2,215 but volume was also lower at 595, compared to Wednesday's 1,040 units.
"Zagrebacka might see a smaller dip now," Hren said.
But he saw space for a further climb of blue chip Pliva pharmaceuticals, which posted excellent 1996 results.
Pliva closed six kuna higher at 480, after trading in a 478.20-483 kuna range, also on diminished volume of 705 units.
Varazdinska Banka, which was recently also listed in the top bracket of Zagreb's bourse, added 998 kuna to 44,000 but sold only three ordinary shares.
The bank's shareholders today approved a 160-to-1 split, after which its shares will be reissued at 100 kuna.
"We know from experience that this should increase the price in the short term," said another trader, Nenad Pavletic from Auctor brokerage.
Hotel Intercontinental led decliners falling 2.94 percent to 165 kuna with 69 shares sold, while the other three active hoteliers traded mixed on extremely meagre volumes.
Confectioner Kras lost 10 kuna to 440 with 379 shares changing hands.
